title: London Pub Quiz

questions.q: Which river flows through the centre of London?
In which year did the Great Fire of London break out?
"Big Ben" is strictly the nickname of what: the tower, the clock, or the great bell?
What is the London Underground's everyday nickname?
Nelson's Column stands in which London square?
Which architect designed St Paul's Cathedral after the Great Fire?
Tradition says a true Cockney is born within the sound of which bells?
The Yeoman Warders at the Tower of London are better known by what nickname?
What is the street address of the Prime Minister's official residence?
London has hosted the Summer Olympics three times. Name all three years.

notes: River Thames; see the River Thames Wikipedia article or the Port of London Authority.
Began 2 September 1666 in Pudding Lane; see Great Fire of London (Wikipedia) or the Museum of London.
UK Parliament's own site says Big Ben is the nickname of the Great Bell; the tower was renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012.
Universal nickname; Transport for London uses 'the Tube' in its own branding.
Nelson's Column, Trafalgar Square; see the Greater London Authority's Trafalgar Square pages.
Wren designed the present St Paul's, completed 1710; see St Paul's Cathedral's own history pages.
Bow Bells of St Mary-le-Bow, Cheapside; see Cockney (Wikipedia) or the church's own site.
Yeoman Warders, nicknamed Beefeaters; see Historic Royal Palaces (Tower of London).
10 Downing Street; see gov.uk 'History of 10 Downing Street'.
1908, 1948, 2012; see the International Olympic Committee's list of host cities.
